newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala Land plans 2 bln-peso long-term debt.
newsitem.headline: Ayala Land plans 2 bln-peso long-term debt.

text.p: Ayala Land Inc plans to issue two billion pesos worth of long-term commercial paper in the next few months to fund capital expenditure for this year, a company official told analysts on Wednesday.
This is on top of the four billion pesos worth of long-term convertible commercial paper the firm issued last month.
The proceeds of the convertible debt as well as the planned new issue will finance Ayala Land's capital expenditure this year which had been set at ten billion pesos, comptroller Jaime Ysmael said.
The bulk of capital expenditure in 1997 will go to land acquisition and the rest to equity investments in units, building construction and commercial center development.
At the meeting, stockholders approved the declassification of the company's Class A and B shares.
Ayala Land officials said this was in line with the ongoing market reforms of the Philippine Stock Exchange that would result in one price for all issued and outstanding shares.
Class B shares of a listed company usually have a higher price at the exchange since only foreigners can buy these shares.
At present, only Ayala Land's B shares are listed. Officials said the company would nowlist the A shares as well.
Foreigners currently own only 12 percent of Ayala Land stock.
Stockholders also approved a 25 percent stock dividend earlier declared by the firm's board. The proposed record date for the stock dividend is on May 8, 1997 and is payable on June 18, 1997.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Philippine Stock Exchange have to clear the stock dividend.
The firm said the 25 percent stock dividend has a value worth 1.449 billion pesos.
